source_evidence.observation: A random variable X satisfying one of properties i–iv of Proposition 2.5.2 is called sub-gaussian.
The sub-gaussian norm of X is defined as the smallest K4 in property iv and is written explicitly as inf {t > 0 : E exp(X²/t²) ≤ 2}.

For a random variable X, the proposition lists four equivalent existential properties: a two-sided Gaussian tail bound, square-root growth of all Lp moments, a local MGF bound for X², and the one-point bound E exp(X²/K4²) ≤ 2, each with a positive parameter Ki.
The parameters in the equivalent properties need not be equal: there is an absolute constant C such that property i with Ki implies property j with some Kj ≤ C Ki.

source_evidence.anchor: Proposition 2.5.2, paragraph beginning ‘Moreover, if E X = 0’ and property (v)
source_evidence.observation: Only under the additional centering condition E X = 0 are properties (i)–(iv) also equivalent to the linear MGF property (v); centering and property (v) are not part of Definition 2.5.6.
The source places the norm on the space of sub-gaussian random variables; it does not define an extended-valued norm for arbitrary random variables in this passage.

binders: X is a random variable (the scalar/real-valued role is structurally indicated by |X|, X², and λX with λ ∈ ℝ in Proposition 2.5.2) [PDF page 13, printed page 24; Proposition 2.5.2].
Each property (i)–(iv) existentially binds its own real parameter Ki > 0 [PDF page 13, printed page 24; Proposition 2.5.2, equivalence sentence and properties (i)–(iv)].
Property (i) universally quantifies t ≥ 0 [PDF page 13, printed page 24; Proposition 2.5.2(i)].
Property (ii) universally quantifies p ≥ 1 [PDF page 13, printed page 24; Proposition 2.5.2(ii)].
Property (iii) universally quantifies λ subject to |λ| ≤ 1/K3 [PDF page 13, printed page 24; Proposition 2.5.2(iii)].
Equation (2.13) takes an infimum over real t > 0 [PDF page 16, printed page 27; Definition 2.5.6, equation (2.13)].
hypotheses: X satisfies at least one of the equivalent properties (i)–(iv) of Proposition 2.5.2, with the positive witness required by that property [PDF page 16, printed page 27; Definition 2.5.6, first sentence; PDF page 13, printed page 24; Proposition 2.5.2(i)–(iv)].

No centering hypothesis E X = 0 is imposed for the sub-gaussian designation or ψ2 norm [PDF page 13, printed page 24; Proposition 2.5.2, ‘Moreover’ clause; PDF page 16, printed page 27; Definition 2.5.6].
conclusions: Such an X is called a sub-gaussian random variable [PDF page 16, printed page 27; Definition 2.5.6, first sentence].
For such X, its sub-gaussian norm is ∥X∥ψ2 = inf {t > 0 : E exp(X²/t²) ≤ 2} [PDF page 16, printed page 27; Definition 2.5.6, equation (2.13)].

The same quantity is described in prose as the smallest admissible K4 in property (iv), whose admissibility condition is K4 > 0 and E exp(X²/K4²) ≤ 2 [PDF page 16, printed page 27; Definition 2.5.6; PDF page 13, printed page 24; Proposition 2.5.2(iv)].
definitions_and_conventions: Property (i): there exists K1 > 0 such that P{|X| ≥ t} ≤ 2 exp(−t²/K1²) for every t ≥ 0 [PDF page 13, printed page 24; Proposition 2.5.2(i)].
Property (ii): there exists K2 > 0 such that ∥X∥Lp = (E|X|^p)^(1/p) ≤ K2√p for every p ≥ 1 [PDF page 13, printed page 24; Proposition 2.5.2(ii)].
Property (iii): there exists K3 > 0 such that E exp(λ²X²) ≤ exp(K3²λ²) for every λ with |λ| ≤ 1/K3 [PDF page 13, printed page 24; Proposition 2.5.2(iii)].
Property (iv): there exists K4 > 0 such that E exp(X²/K4²) ≤ 2 [PDF page 13, printed page 24; Proposition 2.5.2(iv)].

The word ‘equivalent’ permits different witnesses in different properties; the witnesses are comparable only up to an absolute constant factor [PDF page 13, printed page 24; Proposition 2.5.2, opening sentence and footnote 4].
The set-builder expression in (2.13) means the infimum of the positive real scales t satisfying the displayed expectation bound [PDF page 16, printed page 27; Definition 2.5.6, equation (2.13)].
implicit_context: Probability P and expectation E refer to the law/probability space of X [PDF page 13, printed page 24; Proposition 2.5.2(i)–(iv), notation P and E].

The scalar/real-valued nature of X is structural rather than restated in the definition: the referenced proposition uses |X|, real powers and λX for λ ∈ ℝ [PDF page 13, printed page 24; Proposition 2.5.2(i)–(v)].
The ψ2 norm is introduced on sub-gaussian random variables, not as an extended-real quantity on every random variable [PDF page 16, printed page 27; Definition 2.5.6 and Exercise 2.5.7].

Bounds (2.14)–(2.16), which follow the definition, are a later restatement of Proposition 2.5.2 and are not additional clauses of Definition 2.5.6 [PDF page 16, printed page 27; paragraph beginning ‘Let us restate Proposition 2.5.2’].

details: Sub-gaussianity is defined by satisfaction of any one of four equivalent existential properties; it is not defined solely by centered linear-MGF control [PDF page 16, printed page 27; Definition 2.5.6; PDF page 13, printed page 24; Proposition 2.5.2].
The Ki are property-specific existential witnesses and need not be the same numerical value [PDF page 13, printed page 24; Proposition 2.5.2 and footnote 4].
The norm takes an infimum over all admissible positive scales t; it is not an arbitrary chosen property-(iv) witness [PDF page 16, printed page 27; equation (2.13)].
The threshold in the defining exponential-moment inequality is exactly 2, the exponent is X²/t², and the scale restriction is strict t > 0 [PDF page 16, printed page 27; equation (2.13)].
The referenced equivalence is only up to unspecified absolute constant factors, not equality of optimal constants [PDF page 13, printed page 24; Proposition 2.5.2 and footnote 4].

Mean zero is needed only to add property (v) to the equivalence; it is not required for properties (i)–(iv), the sub-gaussian designation, or the ψ2 norm [PDF page 13, printed page 24; Proposition 2.5.2, ‘Moreover’ clause; PDF page 16, printed page 27; Definition 2.5.6].
The defining scale t is strictly positive, so division by t² never uses t = 0 [PDF page 16, printed page 27; equation (2.13)].

As an analyst inference from (2.13), X = 0 has every t > 0 admissible and therefore infimum 0, although there is no smallest positive admissible scale [PDF page 16, printed page 27; Definition 2.5.6 and equation (2.13)].

The selected result is a definition of a class and its norm; it does not itself assert the later quantitative bounds (2.14)–(2.16) or prove the norm axioms requested in Exercise 2.5.7 [PDF page 16, printed page 27; Definition 2.5.6, Exercise 2.5.7, and following restatement paragraph].

undebatable_constraints: The object is a random variable X, and the definition applies when X satisfies any one of properties (i)–(iv) of Proposition 2.5.2 [PDF page 16, printed page 27; Definition 2.5.6].
The ψ2 norm is exactly the infimum over positive t satisfying E exp(X²/t²) ≤ 2 [PDF page 16, printed page 27; equation (2.13)].

The positivity restriction t > 0, the square on both X and t, the exponential, the expectation, the inequality direction ≤, and the numerical threshold 2 must all be preserved [PDF page 16, printed page 27; equation (2.13)].
Sub-gaussianity under this definition does not require E X = 0; centering pertains only to the additional property (v) [PDF page 13, printed page 24; Proposition 2.5.2, ‘Moreover’ clause].

Properties (i)–(iv) are existential in positive, property-specific parameters, and their equivalence is only up to an absolute constant factor [PDF page 13, printed page 24; Proposition 2.5.2 and footnote 4].

The result must not be enlarged to include the later bounds (2.14)–(2.16) as definitional conjuncts or a proof of the norm axioms from Exercise 2.5.7 [PDF page 16, printed page 27; Definition 2.5.6 and immediately following material].

ambiguities.issue: The prose says ‘smallest K4’ while equation (2.13) uses an infimum, and an infimum need not be a smallest positive admissible scale.
ambiguities.evidence: Definition 2.5.6 first calls the norm the ‘smallest K4 in property iv’ and then says ‘In other words’ before equation (2.13), which is an infimum over t > 0 [PDF page 16, printed page 27; Definition 2.5.6 and equation (2.13)].
ambiguities.impact: Equation (2.13) should govern the formal contract: do not add an attainment requirement. This matters already for the degenerate variable X = 0, where the infimum is 0 but no positive admissible scale is least.

ambiguities.issue: The passage does not explicitly specify an extended-real convention for the infimum when applied to a non-sub-gaussian random variable.
ambiguities.evidence: The text first restricts attention to X satisfying properties (i)–(iv), then defines the norm of X, and Exercise 2.5.7 refers to the space of sub-gaussian random variables [PDF page 16, printed page 27; Definition 2.5.6 and Exercise 2.5.7].
ambiguities.impact: The contract should treat the norm as defined here for sub-gaussian X and should not infer a source claim assigning +∞ or another value to arbitrary non-sub-gaussian variables.

ambiguities.issue: The phrase ‘random variable’ is not retyped explicitly as real-valued in Definition 2.5.6.
ambiguities.evidence: The referenced Proposition 2.5.2 uses |X|, X², real Lp moments, and λX with λ ∈ ℝ [PDF page 13, printed page 24; Proposition 2.5.2(i)–(v)].
ambiguities.impact: A real scalar random variable is the structurally supported reading, but the source passage itself does not provide an explicit probability-space or measurability signature.

contract_plain_english: Definition 2.5.6 calls a random variable X sub-gaussian when it satisfies any one of the four equivalent conditions in Proposition 2.5.2: Gaussian-type two-sided tails, √p growth of all Lp moments, a local exponential-moment bound for X², or a one-point exponential-moment bound for X². No mean-zero assumption is required. For such X, its ψ2 norm is the infimum of all positive real scales t for which E exp(X²/t²) ≤ 2. The infimum formula, rather than literal attainment of a smallest positive scale, is the precise definition.
